decision: Start actual APIs from two disposable Git worktrees using the same default session name
why: Prove the existing session boundaries on native macOS before changing the launcher
result: different verified PIDs, ports, main bot IDs, data and project paths

decision: Reproduce dev.py run refusing macOS without omabox
why: The isolated Linux GUI backend cannot launch on this host
result: native Mac development launch path needed

decision: Keep the existing api and desktop commands for host development
why: Session already owns isolated state and lifecycle; a second native coordinator would duplicate that ownership
result: same two commands in each worktree; run remains the Linux omabox command

decision: Derive Mac bundle identity from checkout path, session name, and state path
why: The Mac must distinguish equal session names and equal checkout basenames
result: stable bundle ID across rebuilds; short identity suffix in visible labels

decision: Publish copied executables and plists into immutable hash directories
why: A Cargo rebuild must not replace a running app; independent sessions need no shared lock
result: atomic directory rename publishes a complete bundle; repeat publication reuses it

decision: Set the development window title only on Darwin
why: Keep the Linux window class and title defaults used by omabox

decision: Drive category creation in each native window
why: Prove actual desktop input reaches only the corresponding API
result: each API contains only its own category; foreign owner tokens return 401 both ways

decision: Close A desktop and restart A API while B runs a provider turn
why: Prove independent lifecycle and provider orphan sweep boundaries
result: A preserves its main bot and category; B retains API PID, URL, desktop, and active turn

decision: Rebuild A through dev.py desktop with a shared target canary
why: Prove the normal Cargo path stays private and app publication survives a real rebuild
result: A uses a new immutable copy and refreshed API port; B process, profile, executable inode, and turn stay unchanged

decision: Stop B through its native shortcut and close its window
why: Prove B remains controllable after A rebuilds and closes independently
result: turn is interrupted; closing B leaves A desktop and both APIs running

decision: Fix the reviewed documentation contradictions and disposable preference residue
why: macOS cfprefsd writes bundle preferences outside the private HOME
result: shared publisher launches a real app; native close stops its API and removes its preference domain

decision: Run the portable harness checks on native macOS and Linux arm64
why: Keep the existing development and verification contracts portable
result: Mac 18 development checks and 8 verification checks pass; Linux 17 development checks pass with 1 Mac-only skip and 8 verification checks pass; desktop cargo check passes

decision: Remove only the two generated worktrees and owned processes and preferences
why: Leave the existing installation and unrelated worktrees alone
result: both APIs and desktops exit; generated worktrees, private homes, caches, and preference domains removed

decision: Use the host toolchain homes with the disposable API HOME
why: The first real Cargo rebuild could not find a default Rust toolchain under the fixture HOME
result: fixture sets CARGO_HOME and RUSTUP_HOME; the unmodified development build path then succeeds

decision: Seed a preference in the owned verification bundle domain before interruption
why: An absence check alone could miss a cleanup path that never ran
result: preference exists before SIGTERM and is absent afterward; API, desktop, and disposable data are removed
